title: Richard Carapaz to miss Giro d’Italia after surgery on perineal cyst
content:
Last year’s third-place finisher, Richard Carapaz, will miss next month’s Giro d’Italia after suffering complications following surgery on a perineal cyst this month.

The Ecuadorian rider, 32, will instead now lead EF Education-EasyPost at the Tour de France in July.

“For me, it’s a complete disappointment, because the Giro is a race that I’ve always had a lot of affection for and looked forward to,” Carapaz said in a team statement on Wednesday. “I always want to prepare for it in the best way. Every time I go to the Giro, it is a very special moment. Finding myself in this situation is frustrating because you put a lot of desire and time into it, but in the end I have to prioritize my health now and move forward.

“These are things you aren’t prepared for. I will make the best of it and move forward. We are at the gates of the Tour. The start is less than 70 days away. I want to do super well, prepare for it, and try to get a good result.”

Team doctor Jon Greenwell said: “Because the wound from the surgery was quite big, the recovery was longer than we’d originally predicted, so we decided the timeline to get him ready for the Giro was going to be too short.

“Rather than have him go there, not 100 percent, and potentially have any complications, we thought it would be more sensible to have a good buildup toward the Tour de France and make sure he gets there in the absolute best shape.”

Carapaz’s withdrawal, following UAE Team Emirates’ Joao Almeida and Soudal-Quickstep’s Mikel Landa pulling out on Monday, further weakens the pool of pink jersey contenders.

Visma-Lease a Bike’s Jonas Vingegaard is the overwhelming favourite to complete his set of Grand Tours, with Red Bull-BORA-Hansgrohe’s young Italian climber Giulio Pellizzari expected to be his primary rival.

Though his results had not shone so far this season, Carapaz was in similarly indifferent form before last year’s Giro, where he was arguably the race’s best rider on pure climbing stages.

Trailing pink jersey Isaac del Toro by just 43 seconds ahead of the decisive climb of the Colle delle Finestre, both riders were overhauled by an inspired Simon Yates after remaining overly watchful of the other and failing to respond to the Englishman’s attacks.

He previously won the Giro in 2019 and finished on the Tour podium in 2021. The Giro begins in Bulgaria on May 8 before concluding in Rome on May 31.
